read_prompt: Read the image file {path}. It is an enlarged crop of a few printed lines from one column of an 1854 Hebrew-English lexicon (Gesenius, Robinson translation). Transcribe every complete printed text line exactly, one array element per printed line, top to bottom. Preserve spelling, capitalisation, punctuation, printed abbreviations, section marks and end-of-line hyphenation. Hebrew, Aramaic, Arabic, Syriac, Greek and Ethiopic must be Unicode text with every visible vowel point, dagesh, shin or sin dot, accent and diacritic, and with no point that is not printed; write them in logical order with no bidi control characters, keep the words of a right-to-left phrase in the order they are read, and keep the printed left-to-right order of separate items in a list. Transcribe the letters actually printed even when they are not the dictionary spelling: never insert or drop a vav or yod, and never replace a form with a more familiar one. Distinguish Arabic from Syriac by the letter shapes. If a line is only partially visible at the top or bottom edge, omit it entirely rather than guessing. Never add, reorder, translate, normalise or omit anything that is fully visible. If the crop contains no text, return an empty array.

Syr. ܐܶܟܰܦ. Once Prov. 16, 26 כִּי אָכַף
lines.draft: Syr. ܐܶܟܰܦ. Once Prov. 16, 26 כִּי אָכַף
lines.reread: Syr. ܐܳܟ̇ܦ.  Once Prov. 16, 26 כִּי אָכַף
lines.note: The Syriac word carries two Western vowel signs, one above the alaph (rbasa) and a second distinct sign above the kaph (pthaha), with no plain dot anywhere; Reading B's zqapha on alaph plus a bare dot over kaph does not match the two shaped vowel marks printed. The Hebrew אָכַף (qamets, patah) is identical in both and matches the print.

lines.text: עָלָיו פִּיהוּ for his mouth urges him on,
i. e. his hunger drives him to labour.
The construction with עַל is to be ex-
plained from the primary signif. of lay-
ing on a load.
אֶכֶף m. a load, burden; hence me-
taph. weight, dignity, authority, like
כָּבוֹד. Job 33, 7 וְאַכְפִּי עָלֶיךָ לֹא יִכְבָּד and
lines.draft: כָּבוֹד. Job 33, 7 וְאַכְפִּי עָלֶיךָ לֹא יִכְבָּד and
lines.reread: כָּבוֹד. Job 33, 7 וְאַכְפִּי עָלֶיךָ לֹא יִכְבַּד and
lines.note: The vowel under the dageshed bet of the last Hebrew word is a qamets (horizontal with a descending tick), not a pathach; this matches the Masoretic reading יִכְבָּד in Job 33:7. All other points agree in both readings.

lines.text: my dignity shall not weigh heavy upon
thee. So Chald. Syr. But Sept. ἡ χείρ
μου, and so Kimchi, regarding אֶכֶף i. q.
כַּף in the similar passage Job 13, 21.
The former sense is to be preferred.
* אָכַר a root not in use, i. q. Arab.
lines.draft: * אָכַר a root not in use, i. q. Arab.
lines.reread: * אָבַר a root not in use, i. q. Arab.
lines.note: Second letter is a kaf: its base is flush with the top stroke with no rightward heel protruding past the body as a bet would have; this agrees with the following Arabic cognate أكر (kaf) and the entry’s sense “to dig” (אִכָּר husbandman).

lines.text: أَكَرَ Conj. V, to dig, espec. the earth;
lines.draft: أَكَرَ Conj. V, to dig, espec. the earth;
lines.reread: تَأَكَّرَ Conj. V, to dig, espec. the earth;
lines.note: The printed Arabic has only three letters — alif (with hamza and fatha), kaf, ra — with simple fathas above; there is no initial tāʾ and no shadda on the kāf, so Reading B's تَأَكَّرَ is not what is printed.
